inline DrawIndexedInstanced originalIndexedInstanced=nullptr;
inline DrawAuto originalAuto=nullptr;
inline DrawIndirect originalIndirect=nullptr, originalIndexedIndirect=nullptr;
inline std::atomic<unsigned> submitted{0}, rejected{0};
inline void* installedTargets[7]{};
inline constexpr std::size_t drawSlots[]={12,13,20,21,38,39,40};
inline thread_local bool inVisualDraw=false;
// The katana replacement suppresses only the original item's GPU draws on the
// same context, and only while its own draw is occlusion-verified visible.
inline thread_local ID3D11DeviceContext* katanaSuppress=nullptr;
// Optional read-only observer scoped to the local-player renderer.
using PlayerObserver=void (*)(ID3D11DeviceContext*);
inline std::atomic<PlayerObserver> playerObserver{nullptr};
using ReplayBegin=bool (*)(ID3D11DeviceContext*);
using ReplayEnd=void (*)(ID3D11DeviceContext*);
inline std::atomic<ReplayBegin> replayBegin{nullptr};
inline std::atomic<ReplayEnd> replayEnd{nullptr};
inline thread_local bool inPlayerCapture=false;
// Only while the existing world hat is submitted; off by default.
inline thread_local bool inHatCapture=false;
inline thread_local ID3D11DeviceContext* expectedContext=nullptr;
inline thread_local ID3D11DepthStencilView* expectedDepth=nullptr;
inline thread_local D3D11_COMPARISON_FUNC worldCompare=D3D11_COMPARISON_LESS_EQUAL;
inline thread_local float opacity=1.f;

template<class T> void release(T*& p) { if (p) { p->Release(); p=nullptr; } }
struct Guard {
 ID3D11DeviceContext* ctx=nullptr;
 ID3D11DepthStencilState* oldDepth=nullptr; ID3D11DepthStencilState* newDepth=nullptr;
 ID3D11BlendState* oldBlend=nullptr; ID3D11BlendState* newBlend=nullptr;
 UINT stencil=0, sampleMask=0xffffffffu; FLOAT oldFactor[4]{};
 bool active=false;
 explicit Guard(ID3D11DeviceContext* c) : ctx(c) {
  if (!ctx || ctx!=expectedContext || !expectedDepth) return;
  ID3D11DepthStencilView* current=nullptr; ctx->OMGetRenderTargets(0,nullptr,&current);
  bool same=current && current==expectedDepth; release(current); if (!same) return;
  ctx->OMGetDepthStencilState(&oldDepth,&stencil);
  ctx->OMGetBlendState(&oldBlend,oldFactor,&sampleMask);
  D3D11_DEPTH_STENCIL_DESC depth{};
  if (oldDepth) oldDepth->GetDesc(&depth);
  else {
   depth.StencilReadMask=D3D11_DEFAULT_STENCIL_READ_MASK; depth.StencilWriteMask=D3D11_DEFAULT_STENCIL_WRITE_MASK;
   depth.FrontFace={D3D11_STENCIL_OP_KEEP,D3D11_STENCIL_OP_KEEP,D3D11_STENCIL_OP_KEEP,D3D11_COMPARISON_ALWAYS};
   depth.BackFace=depth.FrontFace;
  }
  depth.DepthEnable=TRUE; depth.DepthWriteMask=D3D11_DEPTH_WRITE_MASK_ZERO;
  depth.DepthFunc=worldCompare; depth.StencilEnable=FALSE;
  D3D11_BLEND_DESC blend{};
  if (oldBlend) oldBlend->GetDesc(&blend);
  else for (auto& target:blend.RenderTarget) {
   target.SrcBlend=D3D11_BLEND_ONE; target.DestBlend=D3D11_BLEND_ZERO; target.BlendOp=D3D11_BLEND_OP_ADD;
   target.SrcBlendAlpha=D3D11_BLEND_ONE; target.DestBlendAlpha=D3D11_BLEND_ZERO; target.BlendOpAlpha=D3D11_BLEND_OP_ADD;
   target.RenderTargetWriteMask=D3D11_COLOR_WRITE_ENABLE_ALL;
  }
  auto& target=blend.RenderTarget[0]; target.BlendEnable=TRUE;
  target.SrcBlend=D3D11_BLEND_BLEND_FACTOR; target.DestBlend=D3D11_BLEND_INV_BLEND_FACTOR;
  target.BlendOp=D3D11_BLEND_OP_ADD; target.SrcBlendAlpha=D3D11_BLEND_ONE;
  target.DestBlendAlpha=D3D11_BLEND_INV_SRC_ALPHA; target.BlendOpAlpha=D3D11_BLEND_OP_ADD;
  ID3D11Device* device=nullptr; ctx->GetDevice(&device);
  if (device) {
   HRESULT d=device->CreateDepthStencilState(&depth,&newDepth);
   HRESULT b=SUCCEEDED(d) ? device->CreateBlendState(&blend,&newBlend) : E_FAIL;
   release(device);
   if (SUCCEEDED(d) && SUCCEEDED(b) && newDepth && newBlend) {
    const FLOAT factor[4]={opacity,opacity,opacity,opacity};
    ctx->OMSetDepthStencilState(newDepth,stencil);
    ctx->OMSetBlendState(newBlend,factor,sampleMask);
    active=true;
   }
  }
 }
 ~Guard() {
  if (active) { ctx->OMSetDepthStencilState(oldDepth,stencil); ctx->OMSetBlendState(oldBlend,oldFactor,sampleMask); }
  release(newBlend); release(oldBlend); release(newDepth); release(oldDepth);
 }
};
template<class Call> void draw(ID3D11DeviceContext* ctx,Call call,bool replayable=false) {
 if (!inVisualDraw) {
  if (ctx && ctx==katanaSuppress) return;
  if (inPlayerCapture) { auto observer=playerObserver.load(std::memory_order_acquire); if (observer) observer(ctx); }
  call(); // The normal world draw is always submitted exactly once first.
  if (inPlayerCapture && replayable) {
   auto begin=replayBegin.load(std::memory_order_acquire); auto end=replayEnd.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
   if (begin && end && begin(ctx)) {
    // Do not recursively observe/replay if the runtime issues another draw
    // while processing this copied call.
    struct Restore { ID3D11DeviceContext* ctx; ReplayEnd end; ~Restore() { end(ctx); inPlayerCapture=true; } } restore{ctx,end};
    inPlayerCapture=false;
    call(); // Only direct Draw/DrawIndexed, including instanced variants.
   }
  }
  return;
 }
 Guard guard(ctx);
 if (!guard.active) { rejected.fetch_add(1,std::memory_order_relaxed); return; }
 submitted.fetch_add(1,std::memory_order_relaxed); call();
 // Copy the *already submitted* hat into the pending player target while the
 // same depth/blend guard is active. Never issue an extra world draw.
 if (inHatCapture && replayable) {
  auto begin=replayBegin.load(std::memory_order_acquire); auto end=replayEnd.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
  if (begin && end && begin(ctx)) {
   struct Restore { ID3D11DeviceContext* ctx; ReplayEnd end; ~Restore() { end(ctx); inHatCapture=true; } } restore{ctx,end};
   inHatCapture=false;
   call();
  }
 }
}
inline void STDMETHODCALLTYPE onDraw(ID3D11DeviceContext* c,UINT n,UINT start) {
 draw(c,[&]{ originalDraw(c,n,start); },true);
}
inline void STDMETHODCALLTYPE onIndexed(ID3D11DeviceContext* c,UINT n,UINT start,INT base) {
 draw(c,[&]{ originalIndexed(c,n,start,base); },true);
}
inline void STDMETHODCALLTYPE onInstanced(ID3D11DeviceContext* c,UINT n,UINT instances,UINT start,UINT first) {
 draw(c,[&]{ originalInstanced(c,n,instances,start,first); },true);
}
inline void STDMETHODCALLTYPE onIndexedInstanced(ID3D11DeviceContext* c,UINT n,UINT instances,UINT start,INT base,UINT first) {
 draw(c,[&]{ originalIndexedInstanced(c,n,instances,start,base,first); },true);
}
inline void STDMETHODCALLTYPE onAuto(ID3D11DeviceContext* c) { draw(c,[&]{ originalAuto(c); }); }
inline void STDMETHODCALLTYPE onIndirect(ID3D11DeviceContext* c,ID3D11Buffer* b,UINT off) {
 draw(c,[&]{ originalIndirect(c,b,off); });
}
inline void STDMETHODCALLTYPE onIndexedIndirect(ID3D11DeviceContext* c,ID3D11Buffer* b,UINT off) {
 draw(c,[&]{ originalIndexedIndirect(c,b,off); });
}
template<class Create,class Enable,class Disable,class Remove>
bool install(ID3D11DeviceContext* ctx,Create create,Enable enable,Disable disable,Remove remove) {
 if (!ctx) return false;
 auto** vtable=*reinterpret_cast<void***>(ctx);
 if (!vtable) return false;
 // ID3D11DeviceContext vtable indices from the D3D11 interface declaration.
 visual_hooks::Hook hooks[]={
  {vtable[12],reinterpret_cast<void*>(&onIndexed),reinterpret_cast<void**>(&originalIndexed)},
  {vtable[13],reinterpret_cast<void*>(&onDraw),reinterpret_cast<void**>(&originalDraw)},
  {vtable[20],reinterpret_cast<void*>(&onIndexedInstanced),reinterpret_cast<void**>(&originalIndexedInstanced)},
  {vtable[21],reinterpret_cast<void*>(&onInstanced),reinterpret_cast<void**>(&originalInstanced)},
  {vtable[38],reinterpret_cast<void*>(&onAuto),reinterpret_cast<void**>(&originalAuto)},
  {vtable[39],reinterpret_cast<void*>(&onIndexedIndirect),reinterpret_cast<void**>(&originalIndexedIndirect)},
  {vtable[40],reinterpret_cast<void*>(&onIndirect),reinterpret_cast<void**>(&originalIndirect)}
 };
 for (std::size_t i=0;i<7;++i) {
  if (!hooks[i].target) return false;
  for (std::size_t j=0;j<i;++j) if (hooks[i].target==hooks[j].target) return false;
 }
 if (!visual_hooks::install(hooks,7,create,enable,disable,remove)) return false;
 for (std::size_t i=0;i<7;++i) installedTargets[i]=hooks[i].target;
 return true;
}
inline bool matches(ID3D11DeviceContext* ctx) {
 if (!ctx) return false;
 auto** vtable=*reinterpret_cast<void***>(ctx);
 if (!vtable) return false;
 for (std::size_t i=0;i<7;++i) if (!installedTargets[i] || vtable[drawSlots[i]]!=installedTargets[i]) return false;
 return true;
}
}

#pragma once
namespace visual_depth_policy {
// Strict mode fails closed if the world pass or scoped draw hooks are missing.
inline bool worldDraw(bool strict,bool worldHook,bool gpuHooks,bool context,bool depthView,bool validCompare) {
 return strict && worldHook && gpuHooks && context && depthView && validCompare;
}
inline bool overlayDraw(bool strict) { return !strict; }
// A diagnostic alternative to the post-entities hat draw, never a fallback to
// the depth-disabled screen path. Both paths must not draw in the same pass.
inline bool playerHat(bool strict,bool selected,bool inEntities,bool local,bool valid,bool attempted) {
 return strict && selected && inEntities && local && valid && !attempted;
}
inline bool entitiesHat(bool selected) { return !selected; }
}

#pragma once
// Read-only candidate discovery while the original local-player renderer is
// executing. Does NOT invoke the renderer again, alter D3D state or read pixels
// back to the CPU. The selected view remains referenced until the UI closes.
#ifdef VISUAL_PLAYER_SKIN_TEST_TYPES
#include VISUAL_PLAYER_SKIN_TEST_TYPES
#else
#include <windows.h>
#include <d3d11.h>
#endif
#include <atomic>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include "visual_skin_policy.h"
namespace visual_player_skin {
struct Candidate { ID3D11ShaderResourceView* view=nullptr; ID3D11Resource* resource=nullptr; UINT width=0,height=0; };
struct Snapshot { ID3D11ShaderResourceView* view=nullptr; UINT width=0,height=0,index=0,count=0; };
inline std::atomic<bool> requested{false};
inline SRWLOCK lock=SRWLOCK_INIT;
inline Candidate candidates[8]{};
inline UINT count=0,selected=0;
inline std::uintptr_t actor=0;
inline ID3D11Device* device=nullptr;
inline std::uint64_t generation=0;
inline thread_local std::uint64_t scopeGeneration=0;
inline thread_local ID3D11DeviceContext* scopeContext=nullptr;
inline void clearLocked() {
 for (auto& c:candidates) { if(c.view)c.view->Release(); if(c.resource)c.resource->Release(); c={}; }
 count=selected=0; actor=0; ++generation; if(device)device->Release(); device=nullptr;
}
inline void setRequested(bool value) {
 bool was=requested.exchange(value,std::memory_order_acq_rel);
 if (was && !value) { AcquireSRWLockExclusive(&lock); clearLocked(); ReleaseSRWLockExclusive(&lock); }
}
inline bool isRequested() { return requested.load(std::memory_order_acquire); }
inline void begin(std::uintptr_t player,ID3D11DeviceContext* ctx) {
 scopeContext=nullptr;
 if (!isRequested() || !ctx || !player) return;
 ID3D11Device* current=nullptr; ctx->GetDevice(&current); if (!current) return;
 bool accepted=false;
 AcquireSRWLockExclusive(&lock);
 if (isRequested()) {
  if (actor!=player || device!=current) { clearLocked(); actor=player; device=current; current=nullptr; }
  scopeGeneration=generation; accepted=true;
 }
 ReleaseSRWLockExclusive(&lock);
 if(current)current->Release();
 if (accepted) scopeContext=ctx;
}
inline void end() { scopeContext=nullptr; }
inline bool colorFormat(DXGI_FORMAT f) {
 switch (f) {
 case DXGI_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_UNORM: case DXGI_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_UNORM_SRGB:
 case DXGI_FORMAT_B8G8R8A8_UNORM: case DXGI_FORMAT_B8G8R8A8_UNORM_SRGB:
 case DXGI_FORMAT_BC1_UNORM: case DXGI_FORMAT_BC1_UNORM_SRGB:
 case DXGI_FORMAT_BC2_UNORM: case DXGI_FORMAT_BC2_UNORM_SRGB:
 case DXGI_FORMAT_BC3_UNORM: case DXGI_FORMAT_BC3_UNORM_SRGB: return true;
 default: return false;
 }
}
inline void observe(ID3D11DeviceContext* ctx) {
 if (!isRequested() || !ctx || ctx!=scopeContext) return;
 ID3D11ShaderResourceView* views[4]{}; ctx->PSGetShaderResources(0,4,views);
 for (auto* view:views) {
  if (!view) continue;
  D3D11_SHADER_RESOURCE_VIEW_DESC vd{}; view->GetDesc(&vd);
  ID3D11Resource* res=nullptr; view->GetResource(&res);
  ID3D11Texture2D* tex=nullptr;
  if (res && vd.ViewDimension==D3D11_SRV_DIMENSION_TEXTURE2D && vd.Texture2D.MostDetailedMip==0 && colorFormat(vd.Format))
   res->QueryInterface(__uuidof(ID3D11Texture2D),reinterpret_cast<void**>(&tex));
  if (tex) {
   D3D11_TEXTURE2D_DESC d{}; tex->GetDesc(&d); tex->Release();
   if (visual_skin_policy::dimensions(d.Width,d.Height,d.SampleDesc.Count,d.ArraySize) && !(d.BindFlags&D3D11_BIND_RENDER_TARGET)) {
    AcquireSRWLockExclusive(&lock);
    bool exists=false; for (UINT i=0;i<count;i++) if (candidates[i].resource==res) { exists=true; break; }
    if (isRequested() && scopeGeneration==generation && !exists && count<8) {
     view->AddRef(); res->AddRef(); candidates[count++]={view,res,d.Width,d.Height};
    }
    ReleaseSRWLockExclusive(&lock);
   }
  }
  if (res) res->Release();
  view->Release();
 }
}
// Caller must Release snapshot.view after ImGui has rendered the frame.
inline Snapshot acquire(ID3D11Device* expected) {
 Snapshot s{}; AcquireSRWLockShared(&lock);
 if (isRequested() && device && device==expected && count) {
  const auto& c=candidates[selected%count]; s={c.view,c.width,c.height,selected%count,count};
  if(s.view)s.view->AddRef();
 }
 ReleaseSRWLockShared(&lock); return s;
}
inline void next() { AcquireSRWLockExclusive(&lock); if (count) selected=(selected+1)%count; ReleaseSRWLockExclusive(&lock); }
}

#pragma once
// Opt-in, best-effort copy of *GPU draws* made by the original local-player
// renderer. It does not call that renderer again. The image has the game's
// current camera, not an independent front view. Experimental, unverified.
#ifdef VISUAL_PLAYER_REPLAY_TEST_TYPES
#include VISUAL_PLAYER_REPLAY_TEST_TYPES
#else
#include <windows.h>
#include <d3d11.h>
#endif
#include <atomic>
#include <cstdint>
#include "visual_model_capture_policy.h"
namespace visual_player_replay {
template<class T> inline void release(T*& p) { if (p) { p->Release(); p=nullptr; } }
struct Target { ID3D11Texture2D* color=nullptr; ID3D11RenderTargetView* rtv=nullptr; ID3D11ShaderResourceView* srv=nullptr; ID3D11Texture2D* depth=nullptr; ID3D11DepthStencilView* dsv=nullptr; };
inline void release(Target& t) { release(t.rtv); release(t.srv); release(t.color); release(t.dsv); release(t.depth); }
inline constexpr UINT size=256;
inline std::atomic<bool> requested{false};
inline SRWLOCK lock=SRWLOCK_INIT;
inline Target targets[2]{};
inline ID3D11Device* device=nullptr;
inline std::uintptr_t actor=0;
inline std::uint64_t generation=0;
inline int front=-1;
inline std::uint64_t lastFrameTick=0;
inline bool creationFailed=false;
inline std::atomic<unsigned> lastDraws{0}, skipped{0};
inline void clearLocked() { for (auto& t:targets) release(t); release(device); actor=0; front=-1; lastFrameTick=0; creationFailed=false; ++generation; lastDraws.store(0); }
inline void setRequested(bool value) {
 bool old=requested.exchange(value,std::memory_order_acq_rel);
 if (old && !value) { AcquireSRWLockExclusive(&lock); clearLocked(); ReleaseSRWLockExclusive(&lock); }
}
inline bool isRequested() { return requested.load(std::memory_order_acquire); }
inline bool createTarget(ID3D11Device* dev,Target& t) {
 D3D11_TEXTURE2D_DESC d{}; d.Width=size; d.Height=size; d.MipLevels=1; d.ArraySize=1;
 d.Format=DXGI_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_UNORM; d.SampleDesc.Count=1; d.Usage=D3D11_USAGE_DEFAULT; d.BindFlags=D3D11_BIND_RENDER_TARGET|D3D11_BIND_SHADER_RESOURCE;
 if (FAILED(dev->CreateTexture2D(&d,nullptr,&t.color)) || FAILED(dev->CreateRenderTargetView(t.color,nullptr,&t.rtv)) || FAILED(dev->CreateShaderResourceView(t.color,nullptr,&t.srv))) { release(t); return false; }
 d.Format=DXGI_FORMAT_D24_UNORM_S8_UINT; d.BindFlags=D3D11_BIND_DEPTH_STENCIL;
 if (FAILED(dev->CreateTexture2D(&d,nullptr,&t.depth)) || FAILED(dev->CreateDepthStencilView(t.depth,nullptr,&t.dsv))) { release(t); return false; }
 return true;
}
// Our private SRVs must not be bound for reading when used as render targets.
// Check all six shader stages once per player pass, before any clear or replay.
inline bool srvBound(ID3D11DeviceContext* c,ID3D11ShaderResourceView* target) {
 using Get = void (STDMETHODCALLTYPE ID3D11DeviceContext::*)(UINT,UINT,ID3D11ShaderResourceView**);
 const Get getters[]={&ID3D11DeviceContext::VSGetShaderResources,&ID3D11DeviceContext::HSGetShaderResources,&ID3D11DeviceContext::DSGetShaderResources,&ID3D11DeviceContext::GSGetShaderResources,&ID3D11DeviceContext::PSGetShaderResources,&ID3D11DeviceContext::CSGetShaderResources};
 bool found=false;
 for (auto get:getters) {
  ID3D11ShaderResourceView* views[D3D11_COMMONSHADER_INPUT_RESOURCE_SLOT_COUNT]{};
  (c->*get)(0,D3D11_COMMONSHADER_INPUT_RESOURCE_SLOT_COUNT,views);
  for (auto*& v:views) { if (v==target) found=true; release(v); }
 }
 return found;
}
struct Scope { ID3D11DeviceContext* ctx=nullptr; ID3D11RenderTargetView* rtv=nullptr; ID3D11DepthStencilView* dsv=nullptr; ID3D11ShaderResourceView* srv=nullptr; int index=-1; std::uint64_t gen=0; unsigned draws=0; bool depthCleared=false, reversedDepth=false; };
inline thread_local Scope scope;
inline void end();
inline bool outputBound(ID3D11DeviceContext* c,ID3D11RenderTargetView* target,ID3D11DepthStencilView* depth) {
 ID3D11RenderTargetView* views[D3D11_SIMULTANEOUS_RENDER_TARGET_COUNT]{}; ID3D11DepthStencilView* dsv=nullptr;
 c->OMGetRenderTargets(D3D11_SIMULTANEOUS_RENDER_TARGET_COUNT,views,&dsv);
 bool found=dsv==depth; for (auto*& v:views) { found|=v==target; release(v); } release(dsv); return found;
}
inline void begin(std::uintptr_t player,ID3D11DeviceContext* ctx) {
 end(); if (!isRequested() || !player || !ctx) return;
 ID3D11Device* current=nullptr; ctx->GetDevice(&current); if (!current) return;
 AcquireSRWLockExclusive(&lock);
 if (isRequested()) {
  if (device!=current || actor!=player) { clearLocked(); device=current; current=nullptr; actor=player; }
  if (!creationFailed && (!targets[0].rtv || !targets[1].rtv)) {
   release(targets[0]); release(targets[1]);
   if (!createTarget(device,targets[0]) || !createTarget(device,targets[1])) { release(targets[0]); release(targets[1]); creationFailed=true; }
  }
  if (targets[0].rtv && targets[1].rtv) {
   const int index=front==0?1:0; auto& t=targets[index];
   scope.ctx=ctx; scope.ctx->AddRef(); scope.rtv=t.rtv; scope.dsv=t.dsv; scope.srv=t.srv; scope.index=index; scope.gen=generation;
   scope.rtv->AddRef(); scope.dsv->AddRef(); scope.srv->AddRef();
  }
 }
 ReleaseSRWLockExclusive(&lock); release(current);
 if (!scope.ctx) return;
 if (srvBound(ctx,scope.srv) || outputBound(ctx,scope.rtv,scope.dsv)) { end(); return; }
 const FLOAT transparent[4]={0,0,0,0}; ctx->ClearRenderTargetView(scope.rtv,transparent);
}
inline void end() {
 if (scope.ctx && scope.draws) {
  AcquireSRWLockExclusive(&lock);
  if (isRequested() && scope.gen==generation) { front=scope.index; lastFrameTick=GetTickCount64(); lastDraws.store(scope.draws,std::memory_order_relaxed); }
  ReleaseSRWLockExclusive(&lock);
 }
 release(scope.rtv); release(scope.dsv); release(scope.srv); release(scope.ctx); scope={};
}
inline ID3D11ShaderResourceView* acquire(ID3D11Device* expected) {
 ID3D11ShaderResourceView* result=nullptr; AcquireSRWLockShared(&lock);
 const auto now=GetTickCount64();
 if (isRequested() && expected && device==expected && front>=0 && lastFrameTick && now>=lastFrameTick && now-lastFrameTick<=2000) { result=targets[front].srv; if(result)result->AddRef(); }
 ReleaseSRWLockShared(&lock); return result;
}
struct DrawState {
 ID3D11DeviceContext* ctx=nullptr;
 ID3D11RenderTargetView* rtv[D3D11_SIMULTANEOUS_RENDER_TARGET_COUNT]{};
 ID3D11DepthStencilView* dsv=nullptr;
 D3D11_VIEWPORT viewport{};
 D3D11_RECT scissors[D3D11_VIEWPORT_AND_SCISSORRECT_OBJECT_COUNT_PER_PIPELINE]{};
 UINT scissorCount=0;
 bool active=false;
};
inline thread_local DrawState saved;
inline bool beginDraw(ID3D11DeviceContext* ctx) {
 if (!isRequested() || !scope.ctx || ctx!=scope.ctx || saved.active || scope.draws>=128) return false;
 UINT count=0; ctx->RSGetViewports(&count,nullptr);
 D3D11_VIEWPORT vp{}; if (count==1) { UINT one=1; ctx->RSGetViewports(&one,&vp); if(one!=1)count=0; }
 visual_model_capture_policy::Viewport input{vp.TopLeftX,vp.TopLeftY,vp.Width,vp.Height,vp.MinDepth,vp.MaxDepth}, output{};
 const bool validVp=count==1 && visual_model_capture_policy::viewport(input,static_cast<float>(size),output);
 ID3D11DepthStencilState* depth=nullptr; UINT stencil=0; ctx->OMGetDepthStencilState(&depth,&stencil);
 D3D11_DEPTH_STENCIL_DESC d{}; if (depth) depth->GetDesc(&d); else { d.DepthEnable=TRUE; d.DepthFunc=D3D11_COMPARISON_LESS; }
 release(depth);
 const bool depthOk=d.DepthEnable && (d.DepthFunc==D3D11_COMPARISON_LESS || d.DepthFunc==D3D11_COMPARISON_LESS_EQUAL || d.DepthFunc==D3D11_COMPARISON_GREATER || d.DepthFunc==D3D11_COMPARISON_GREATER_EQUAL);
 ID3D11RenderTargetView* old[D3D11_SIMULTANEOUS_RENDER_TARGET_COUNT]{}; ID3D11DepthStencilView* oldDsv=nullptr;
 ctx->OMGetRenderTargets(D3D11_SIMULTANEOUS_RENDER_TARGET_COUNT,old,&oldDsv);
 ID3D11Buffer* streams[D3D11_SO_BUFFER_SLOT_COUNT]{}; ctx->SOGetTargets(D3D11_SO_BUFFER_SLOT_COUNT,streams);
 bool so=false; for(auto*& p:streams) { so|=p!=nullptr; release(p); }
 ID3D11Predicate* pred=nullptr; BOOL predValue=FALSE; ctx->GetPredication(&pred,&predValue); const bool predicate=pred!=nullptr; release(pred);
 ID3D11Device* dev=nullptr; ctx->GetDevice(&dev); const bool deviceReady=dev!=nullptr;
 UINT slots=dev && dev->GetFeatureLevel()>=D3D_FEATURE_LEVEL_11_1 ? 64u : 8u; release(dev);
 ID3D11UnorderedAccessView* uavs[64]{}; ctx->OMGetRenderTargetsAndUnorderedAccessViews(0,nullptr,nullptr,0,slots,uavs);
 bool uav=false; for (UINT i=0;i<slots;++i) { uav|=uavs[i]!=nullptr; release(uavs[i]); }
 const bool safe=visual_model_capture_policy::safeDraw(validVp && deviceReady,depthOk && oldDsv!=nullptr,d.StencilEnable!=FALSE,uav,so,predicate,count);
 if (!safe) { for(auto*& p:old)release(p); release(oldDsv); skipped.fetch_add(1,std::memory_order_relaxed); return false; }
 const bool reversed=d.DepthFunc==D3D11_COMPARISON_GREATER || d.DepthFunc==D3D11_COMPARISON_GREATER_EQUAL;
 if (scope.depthCleared && reversed!=scope.reversedDepth) {
  for (auto*& p:old) release(p);
  release(oldDsv); skipped.fetch_add(1,std::memory_order_relaxed); return false;
 }
 if (!scope.depthCleared) {
  ctx->ClearDepthStencilView(scope.dsv,D3D11_CLEAR_DEPTH,reversed?0.f:1.f,0); scope.depthCleared=true; scope.reversedDepth=reversed;
 }
 saved.ctx=ctx; for (UINT i=0;i<D3D11_SIMULTANEOUS_RENDER_TARGET_COUNT;++i) saved.rtv[i]=old[i]; saved.dsv=oldDsv; saved.viewport=vp;
 saved.scissorCount=D3D11_VIEWPORT_AND_SCISSORRECT_OBJECT_COUNT_PER_PIPELINE; ctx->RSGetScissorRects(&saved.scissorCount,saved.scissors);
 D3D11_VIEWPORT dst{output.x,output.y,output.width,output.height,output.minDepth,output.maxDepth};
 const D3D11_RECT rect{0,0,static_cast<LONG>(size),static_cast<LONG>(size)};
 ctx->OMSetRenderTargets(1,&scope.rtv,scope.dsv); ctx->RSSetViewports(1,&dst); ctx->RSSetScissorRects(1,&rect); saved.active=true;
 return true;
}
inline void endDraw(ID3D11DeviceContext* ctx) {
 if (!saved.active || ctx!=saved.ctx) return;
 ctx->OMSetRenderTargets(D3D11_SIMULTANEOUS_RENDER_TARGET_COUNT,saved.rtv,saved.dsv);
 ctx->RSSetViewports(1,&saved.viewport); ctx->RSSetScissorRects(saved.scissorCount,saved.scissorCount?saved.scissors:nullptr);
 for (auto*& p:saved.rtv) release(p);
 release(saved.dsv); saved={}; ++scope.draws;
}
}

#pragma once
#include <cmath>
namespace visual_model_capture_policy {
// This is not a new camera: it magnifies the actor's existing world projection.
struct Viewport { float x,y,width,height,minDepth,maxDepth; };
inline bool viewport(const Viewport& source,float size,Viewport& out) {
 if (!std::isfinite(source.width) || !std::isfinite(source.height) || !std::isfinite(source.minDepth) || !std::isfinite(source.maxDepth) || source.width<1 || source.height<1 || source.minDepth<0 || source.maxDepth>1 || source.minDepth>source.maxDepth || !std::isfinite(size) || size<1 || size>1024) return false;
 const float aspect=source.width/source.height;
 if (!std::isfinite(aspect) || aspect<.2f || aspect>5.f) return false;
 const float h=size*3.f, w=h*aspect;
 out={(size-w)*.5f,(size-h)*.5f,w,h,source.minDepth,source.maxDepth};
 return true;
}
inline bool safeDraw(bool contextOk,bool depthOk,bool stencil,bool outputUav,bool streamOutput,bool predication,unsigned viewportCount) {
 return contextOk && depthOk && !stencil && !outputUav && !streamOutput && !predication && viewportCount==1;
}
}

#pragma once
// Independent, deterministic preview geometry. The game's settings, mesh and
// animation functions are shared, but this is not the game's player model or
// shader. It uses an original, simplified Steve-style sample avatar.
#include "../research/china_hat/hat_mesh.h"
#include "hat_animation.h"
#include "visual_gradient.h"
#include <algorithm>
#include <cmath>
#include <cstdint>

namespace visual_avatar_preview {
struct HatSettings {
 float radius, height, offset, bobAmount, bobSpeed, rainbowSpeed;
 bool gradient;
};
inline bool hat(china_hat::Mesh& mesh,const HatSettings& s,std::uint64_t now) {
 const float phase=s.gradient ? visual_gradient::phase(now,s.rainbowSpeed) : static_cast<float>(now%8000)/8000.f;
 // Sample head has a top at y=.64; use the game's calibrated .03 offset and
 // the exact same bob function/radius/height/phase as the game renderer.
 const china_hat::Point anchor{0.f,.64f+.03f+s.offset+hat_animation::bob(now,s.bobAmount,s.bobSpeed),0.f};
 return china_hat::build(mesh,anchor,s.radius,s.height,48,phase,255);
}
struct Point2 { float x,y; };
inline Point2 project(china_hat::Point p,float scale=125.f) {
 return {140.f+(p.x-p.z*.22f)*scale, 205.f-(p.y+.35f)*scale+p.z*scale*.24f};
}
// Fit the whole bob range once for the current settings. Basing the camera
// scale on the instantaneous hat position makes the *character* pulse as the
// hat moves. Only the hat should bob; fixed settings must yield a fixed scale.
inline float hatScale(const HatSettings& s) {
 const float top=.64f+.03f+s.offset+2.f*std::max(0.f,s.bobAmount)+s.height;
 return std::min({145.f,115.f/(s.radius*1.03f),190.f/std::max(.5f,top+.35f+s.radius*.24f)});
}
inline Point2 trailPoint(float t,std::uint64_t now,float lifetime) {
 t=std::clamp(t,0.f,1.f); const float phase=visual_gradient::phase(now,.18f)*6.28318530718f;
 float length=70.f+110.f*std::clamp((lifetime-1.f)/5.f,0.f,1.f);
 // t=0 is the moving player's position; t=1 is the oldest trail end.
 return {226.f-t*length,183.f+8.f*std::sin(phase+t*4.4f)*t};
}
inline float trailHeight(float normalizedHeight) { return std::clamp(normalizedHeight,.3f,1.f)*80.f; }
}

#pragma once
#include "../research/china_hat/hat_mesh.h"
#include <algorithm>
#include <cmath>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>

namespace visual_gradient {
inline float phase(std::uint64_t ms, float cyclesPerSecond) {
 if (!std::isfinite(cyclesPerSecond) || cyclesPerSecond < 0) return 0.f;
 return static_cast<float>(std::fmod(static_cast<double>(ms)*.001*cyclesPerSecond,1.0));
}
// Samples run from oldest to newest. Geometry interpolation between samples is
// controlled by the game's vertex material; this code does not enable blending.
inline china_hat::Color trail(std::size_t index, std::size_t count, float timePhase, std::uint8_t alpha) {
 if (count < 2 || !std::isfinite(timePhase)) return china_hat::rainbow(0.f,alpha);
 const float position=static_cast<float>(std::min(index,count-1))/static_cast<float>(count-1);
 // Less than a full hue turn so the newest and oldest ends differ.
 return china_hat::rainbow(timePhase + position*.8f,alpha);
}
}

#pragma once
#include <array>
#include <cmath>
#include <cstdint>

namespace visual_color {
enum class Effect { Hat, Trail };
inline std::array<float,4> material(bool enabled,Effect effect) {
 if (!enabled) return {{1.f,1.f,1.f,1.f}};
 return effect==Effect::Hat ? std::array<float,4>{{0.20f,1.f,0.42f,1.f}}
                            : std::array<float,4>{{0.08f,0.86f,1.f,1.f}};
}
// Animate the whole material color; 1.1.5's active material did not honor our
// per-vertex gradient in the user's test. Never imply per-vertex rainbow.
inline std::array<float,4> animated(bool enabled,bool rainbow,std::array<float,3> base,float cyclesPerSecond,std::uint64_t ms) {
 if (!enabled) return {{1.f,1.f,1.f,1.f}};
 if (!rainbow) return {{base[0],base[1],base[2],1.f}};
 double hue=std::fmod(static_cast<double>(ms)*0.001*static_cast<double>(cyclesPerSecond),1.0);
 float x=static_cast<float>(hue*6.0); int sector=static_cast<int>(x); float f=x-sector;
 constexpr float floor=.22f; float rise=floor+(1.f-floor)*f, fall=1.f-(1.f-floor)*f;
 switch (sector) {
  case 0: return {{1.f,rise,floor,1.f}};
  case 1: return {{fall,1.f,floor,1.f}};
  case 2: return {{floor,1.f,rise,1.f}};
  case 3: return {{floor,fall,1.f,1.f}};
  case 4: return {{rise,floor,1.f,1.f}};
  default:return {{1.f,floor,fall,1.f}};
 }
}
}

#pragma once
#include "../research/china_hat/hat_mesh.h"
#include <cmath>
namespace visual_ribbon {
// One vertical trail panel as two triangles, emitted in both orientations.
// Points are already camera-relative. This is geometry only, not a promise
// that the native game accepts the candidate triangle topology/material.
template<class Emit>
bool segment(const china_hat::Vertex& a,const china_hat::Vertex& b,float height,Emit emit) {
 if (!std::isfinite(height) || height<=0 || height>2.0f) return false;
 for (const auto p:{a.position,b.position})
  if (!std::isfinite(p.x) || !std::isfinite(p.y) || !std::isfinite(p.z)) return false;
 auto upperA=a, upperB=b; upperA.position.y+=height; upperB.position.y+=height;
 emit(a); emit(b); emit(upperB); emit(a); emit(upperB); emit(upperA);
 emit(upperB); emit(b); emit(a); emit(upperA); emit(upperB); emit(a);
 return true;
}
}

#pragma once
#include "../research/china_hat/hat_mesh.h"
#include <array>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cmath>

// Bounded history in world space. No platform, input, game or rendering calls.
namespace visual_trail {
struct Sample { china_hat::Point point; std::uint64_t time=0; };
class History {
public:
 static constexpr std::size_t capacity=128;
 static constexpr std::uint64_t lifetime=3000;
 void clear() { count_=0; actor_=0; lastSeen_=0; }
 void update(std::uintptr_t actor, china_hat::Point p, std::uint64_t now, std::uint64_t ttl=lifetime) {
  if (!actor || !std::isfinite(p.x) || !std::isfinite(p.y) || !std::isfinite(p.z)) { clear(); return; }
  if (actor_!=actor || (lastSeen_ && (now<lastSeen_ || now-lastSeen_>1000))) { clear(); actor_=actor; }
  lastSeen_=now; expire(now,ttl);
  if (count_) {
   const auto& last=points_[count_-1];
   float dx=p.x-last.point.x, dy=p.y-last.point.y, dz=p.z-last.point.z;
   float distance2=dx*dx+dy*dy+dz*dz;
   if (!std::isfinite(distance2) || distance2>64.f) { clear(); actor_=actor; lastSeen_=now; }
   else if (distance2<.0025f || now-last.time<50) return;
  }
  if (count_==capacity) { for (std::size_t i=1;i<count_;++i) points_[i-1]=points_[i]; --count_; }
  points_[count_++]={p,now};
 }
 void expire(std::uint64_t now,std::uint64_t ttl=lifetime) {
  std::size_t n=0;
  while (n<count_ && (now<points_[n].time || now-points_[n].time>ttl)) ++n;
  if (n) { for (std::size_t i=n;i<count_;++i) points_[i-n]=points_[i]; count_-=n; }
 }
 std::size_t size() const { return count_; }
 const Sample& operator[](std::size_t i) const { return points_[i]; }
private:
 std::array<Sample,capacity> points_{};
 std::size_t count_=0;
 std::uintptr_t actor_=0;
 std::uint64_t lastSeen_=0;
};
}

#pragma once
#include <cmath>
#include <cstdint>
namespace hat_animation {
// A gentle lift above the calibrated head anchor; period is in milliseconds.
// No accumulated timestep drift and no dependence on frame rate.
inline float bob(std::uint64_t now,float amplitude=.07f,float speed=.3125f) {
 constexpr double tau=6.2831853071795864769;
 const double phase=std::fmod(static_cast<double>(now)*.001*static_cast<double>(speed),1.0);
 return amplitude*(1.0f+static_cast<float>(std::sin(tau*phase)));
}
}

#pragma once
#include "../research/china_hat/hat_mesh.h"
#include <cstddef>
// Emit an independent ring plus evenly spaced apex-to-rim spokes. The caller
// chooses line-list topology/material, and owns all native rendering state.
namespace china_hat {
template<class Emit> bool emitDoubleSidedSurface(const Mesh& mesh, Emit emit) {
 if (mesh.triangleVertices < 24 || mesh.triangleVertices > kMaxSegments*3 || mesh.triangleVertices%3) return false;
 for (std::size_t i=0;i<mesh.triangleVertices;i+=3) {
  emit(mesh.triangles[i]); emit(mesh.triangles[i+1]); emit(mesh.triangles[i+2]);
  emit(mesh.triangles[i]); emit(mesh.triangles[i+2]); emit(mesh.triangles[i+1]);
 }
 return true;
}
template<class Emit> bool emitWireframe(const Mesh& mesh, std::size_t spokes, Emit emit) {
 if (mesh.outlineVertices<9 || mesh.outlineVertices>kMaxSegments+1) return false;
 const std::size_t n=mesh.outlineVertices-1;
 if (!spokes || spokes>n || n%spokes || mesh.triangleVertices!=n*3) return false;
 for (std::size_t i=0;i<n;i++) { emit(mesh.outline[i]); emit(mesh.outline[i+1]); }
 for (std::size_t i=0;i<n;i+=n/spokes) { emit(mesh.triangles[i*3]); emit(mesh.outline[i]); }
 return true;
}
}

#pragma once
#include <cstdint>

// Resolve only the player slot of a recently observed ClientInstance. A
// plausible unrelated actor or the camera target is not evidence of identity.
namespace hat_player {
constexpr std::uintptr_t playerSlot=0x60;
constexpr std::uint64_t maxTickAge=2000;
inline bool alignedPointer(std::uintptr_t value) {
 return value>=0x10000 && value<0x0000800000000000ULL && (value&7)==0;
}
template<class Read>
bool fromClient(std::uintptr_t client,std::uint64_t tick,std::uint64_t now,Read read,std::uintptr_t& player) {
 player=0;
 if (!alignedPointer(client) || !tick || now<tick || now-tick>maxTickAge) return false;
 std::uintptr_t first=0, again=0;
 if (!read(client+playerSlot,first) || !alignedPointer(first) ||
     !read(client+playerSlot,again) || again!=first) return false;
 player=first; return true;
}
}

constexpr std::size_t kImageSize = 0x1a91000;

// User-provided read-only diagnostics for the exact game executable. In
// addition to these signatures, check the complete on-disk SHA-256.
constexpr Signature signatures[] = {

 {0x5b07d0, {0x48,0x89,0x5c,0x24,0x08,0x48,0x89,0x74,0x24,0x10,0x48,0x89,0x7c,0x24,0x18,0x4c}},
 {0x5d0660, {0x48,0x83,0xec,0x68,0x80,0xb9,0x70,0x01,0x00,0x00,0x00,0x45,0x8b,0xd0,0x4c,0x8b}},
 {0x5d0890, {0x80,0xb9,0x24,0x01,0x00,0x00,0x00,0x75,0x69,0x44,0x0f,0xb6,0x54,0x24,0x28,0x41}},

};
// Only hooks installed by the adapter can account for these changed prologues.
// The on-disk signature and executable hash must still be checked separately.
inline bool mayBePatched(std::uint32_t rva, bool visualInstalled, bool worldInstalled) {
 if (!visualInstalled) return false;
 return rva==0x581910 || rva==0x3528c0 || rva==0x11b2d0 || (worldInstalled && rva==0x5ae250);
}
inline bool identity(const std::uint8_t* hash, std::uint32_t timestamp, std::size_t imageSize) {
 return hash && timestamp == kTimestamp && imageSize == kImageSize && std::memcmp(hash,kHash,32)==0;
}

================================================================================
НАЧАЛО ФАЙЛА: repair/src/china_hat_hash.h

#pragma once
#include <algorithm>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <vector>

// BCrypt retains the caller-owned hash object buffer until the hash handle is
// destroyed. Keep storage alive longer than both handles, including on errors
// and exceptions. Api is injectable so this ordering can be tested portably.
template <class Api>
bool hashHatExecutable(Api& api, const std::uint8_t* bytes, std::size_t size, std::uint8_t result[32]) {
    std::vector<std::uint8_t> storage;
    typename Api::Algorithm algorithm{};
    typename Api::Hash hash{};
    struct Cleanup {
        Api& api;
        typename Api::Algorithm& algorithm;
        typename Api::Hash& hash;
        ~Cleanup() {
            if (hash) api.destroyHash(hash);
            if (algorithm) api.closeAlgorithm(algorithm);
        }
    } cleanup{api, algorithm, hash};
    if (!api.openAlgorithm(algorithm)) return false;
    std::uint32_t objectSize=0, hashSize=0;
    if (!api.objectLength(algorithm,objectSize) || objectSize==0 || objectSize>=65536 ||
        !api.hashLength(algorithm,hashSize) || hashSize!=32) return false;
    storage.resize(objectSize);
    if (!api.createHash(algorithm,hash,storage.data(),objectSize)) return false;
    for (std::size_t pos=0;pos<size;) {
        auto chunk=static_cast<std::uint32_t>(std::min<std::size_t>(size-pos,1024*1024));
        if (!api.hashData(hash,bytes+pos,chunk)) return false;
        pos+=chunk;
    }
    return api.finishHash(hash,result,32);
}

#pragma once
#include <cstddef>

// MinHook operations are injected for portable rollback tests. Do not remove
// a trampoline when disabling its active hook failed.
namespace visual_hooks {
struct Hook { void* target; void* detour; void** original; bool created=false; bool active=false; };
template<class Create,class Enable,class Disable,class Remove>
bool install(Hook* hooks,std::size_t count,Create create,Enable enable,Disable disable,Remove remove) {
 bool success=true;
 for (std::size_t i=0;i<count;++i) {
  if (create(hooks[i].target,hooks[i].detour,hooks[i].original)!=0) { success=false; break; }
  hooks[i].created=true;
 }
 if (success) for (std::size_t i=0;i<count;++i) {
  if (enable(hooks[i].target)!=0) { success=false; break; }
  hooks[i].active=true;
 }
 if (!success) for (std::size_t i=0;i<count;++i) {
  auto& hook=hooks[i];
  if (hook.active && disable(hook.target)==0) hook.active=false;
  if (hook.created && !hook.active) remove(hook.target);
 }
 return success;
}
}

#pragma once
// Standalone experimental cone mesh. No Minecraft hooks, memory access, or
// rendering side effects. The caller must supply the interpolated world-space
// position of the head, relative to the render origin; the game-specific
// camera/model binding for 1.1.5 is not yet established.
#include <array>
#include <cmath>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>

namespace china_hat {
struct Point { float x, y, z; };
struct Color { std::uint8_t r, g, b, a; };
struct Vertex { Point position; Color color; };
constexpr std::size_t kMaxSegments = 96;
struct Mesh {
    // A triangle list is usable by either a game's tessellator or a GPU buffer.
    std::array<Vertex, kMaxSegments * 3> triangles{};
    std::array<Vertex, kMaxSegments + 1> outline{};
    std::size_t triangleVertices = 0, outlineVertices = 0;
};
inline Color rainbow(float hue, std::uint8_t alpha) {
    hue = hue - std::floor(hue);
    float t = hue * 6.0f;
    int sector = static_cast<int>(t);
    float f = t - static_cast<float>(sector);
    auto scale = [](float v) { return static_cast<std::uint8_t>(std::lround(v * 255.0f)); };
    const float dim = 0.22f, mid = dim + (1.0f - dim) * f, inv = 1.0f - (1.0f - dim) * f;
    switch (sector) {
    case 0: return {255, scale(mid), scale(dim), alpha};
    case 1: return {scale(inv), 255, scale(dim), alpha};
    case 2: return {scale(dim), 255, scale(mid), alpha};
    case 3: return {scale(dim), scale(inv), 255, alpha};
    case 4: return {scale(mid), scale(dim), 255, alpha};
    default: return {255, scale(dim), scale(inv), alpha};
    }
}
// Start empty on invalid input. Explicit limits prevent huge / nonfinite world
// camera-relative coordinates from generating invalid vertices. Subtract the
// render origin before calling, so distant world positions keep float precision.
// phase is cycles, not seconds.
inline bool build(Mesh& out, Point head, float radius, float height,
                  std::size_t segments, float phase, std::uint8_t alpha = 160) {
    out.triangleVertices = out.outlineVertices = 0;
    if (!std::isfinite(head.x) || !std::isfinite(head.y) || !std::isfinite(head.z) ||
        std::fabs(head.x) > 32768.0f || std::fabs(head.y) > 32768.0f || std::fabs(head.z) > 32768.0f ||
        !std::isfinite(radius) || !std::isfinite(height) || !std::isfinite(phase) ||
        radius <= 0.0f || radius > 2.0f || height <= 0.0f || height > 2.0f ||
        segments < 8 || segments > kMaxSegments) return false;
    constexpr float tau = 6.2831853071795864769f;
    // Reduce before adding fractions so very large phases cannot overflow.
    phase -= std::floor(phase);
    const Point apex{head.x, head.y + height, head.z};
    auto rim = [&](std::size_t i) {
        float turn = static_cast<float>(i % segments) / static_cast<float>(segments);
        float angle = tau * turn;
        return Vertex{{head.x + radius * std::cos(angle), head.y,
                       head.z + radius * std::sin(angle)}, rainbow(turn + phase, alpha)};
    };
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < segments; ++i) {
        Vertex a = rim(i), b = rim(i + 1);
        // Winding is consistent around the cone. Material/depth configuration
        // is deliberately left to the eventual game-specific renderer.
        out.triangles[i * 3] = {apex, rainbow(phase + (static_cast<float>(i) + 0.5f) / segments, alpha)};
        out.triangles[i * 3 + 1] = a;
        out.triangles[i * 3 + 2] = b;
        out.outline[i] = a;
    }
    out.outline[segments] = out.outline[0];
    out.triangleVertices = segments * 3;
    out.outlineVertices = segments + 1;
    return true;
}
}

#pragma once

// Windows cursor and client rectangle must be expressed in the same coordinate
// system. ImGui's legacy bridge later scales these values to the back buffer.
// Do not clamp: an outside cursor must remain outside the overlay as well.
inline bool client_pointer(float cursorX, float cursorY, float clientWidth, float clientHeight,
                           float& x, float& y, float& w, float& h) {
    if (clientWidth <= 0.0f || clientHeight <= 0.0f) return false;
    x = cursorX; y = cursorY; w = clientWidth; h = clientHeight;
    return true;
}

// CoreWindow bounds are in the same DIPs as PointerPosition. Bounds origin
// describes the client origin inside the system window (e.g. its title bar).
inline bool uwp_client_pointer(float pointerX, float pointerY, float left, float top,
                               float width, float height, float& x, float& y, float& w, float& h) {
    return client_pointer(pointerX - left, pointerY - top, width, height, x, y, w, h);
}

// x64 1.1.5 input research adapter. Observed from the user's exact executable,
// not an imported x86 layout. Game hooks stay dormant if identity or byte
// signatures differ. The actual game behavior still needs Windows testing.
#define WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN
#define NOMINMAX
#include <windows.h>
#include <atomic>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstring>
#include "menu_mouse_native.h"
#include "menu_mouse_policy.h"
#include "visual_hooks.h"

namespace {
constexpr std::uintptr_t queueRva=0x6f0f30, tickRva=0x7d37f0, factoryRva=0x7d6370;
constexpr std::uintptr_t mouseVtableRva=0x1738e28;
struct Signature { std::uintptr_t rva; unsigned char bytes[16]; };
constexpr Signature signatures[]={
 {queueRva,{0x48,0x89,0x54,0x24,0x10,0x57,0x48,0x83,0xec,0x30,0x48,0xc7,0x44,0x24,0x20,0xfe}},
 {tickRva,{0x48,0x8b,0xc4,0x55,0x57,0x41,0x54,0x41,0x56,0x41,0x57,0x48,0x8b,0xec,0x48,0x83}},
 {factoryRva,{0x48,0x89,0x5c,0x24,0x10,0x48,0x89,0x74,0x24,0x18,0x48,0x89,0x7c,0x24,0x20,0x41}},
 {0x7d3b72,{0x8b,0x43,0x74,0x83,0xf8,0x01,0x75,0x10,0x80,0x7b,0x72,0x00,0x75,0x0a,0x48,0x8b}},
 {0x7d4590,{0x40,0x53,0x56,0x57,0x41,0x56,0x48,0x83,0xec,0x38,0x48,0xc7,0x44,0x24,0x20,0xfe}},
 {0x7d4850,{0x40,0x53,0x56,0x57,0x41,0x56,0x48,0x83,0xec,0x38,0x48,0xc7,0x44,0x24,0x20,0xfe}}
};
using QueueFn=void (*)(void*,void**);
using TickFn=std::uintptr_t (*)(void*);
using FactoryFn=void** (*)(void**,const unsigned char*,const unsigned char*,const std::uint32_t*,const std::int16_t*,const std::int16_t*);
using DeleteFn=void (*)(void*,unsigned);
QueueFn realQueue=nullptr; TickFn realTick=nullptr; FactoryFn factory=nullptr;
std::uintptr_t image=0;
std::atomic<bool> menuOpen{false}, ready{false};
std::atomic<unsigned> held{0};
// The cursor state is used only on the game's live input-tick thread. No
// handler or CoreWindow pointer is retained between ticks.
thread_local menu_mouse::CursorPolicy cursor;

bool read(const void* address,void* dst,std::size_t n) {
 SIZE_T got=0; return address && ReadProcessMemory(GetCurrentProcess(),address,dst,n,&got) && got==n;
}
template<class T> bool readAt(const void* base,std::size_t offset,T& out) {
 return base && read(static_cast<const unsigned char*>(base)+offset,&out,sizeof(out));
}
bool writable(void* p,std::size_t n) {
 MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION m{};
 if (!p || !VirtualQuery(p,&m,sizeof(m)) || m.State!=MEM_COMMIT || (m.Protect&(PAGE_GUARD|PAGE_NOACCESS))) return false;
 DWORD prot=m.Protect&0xff;
 if (prot!=PAGE_READWRITE && prot!=PAGE_WRITECOPY && prot!=PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE && prot!=PAGE_EXECUTE_WRITECOPY) return false;
 auto x=reinterpret_cast<std::uintptr_t>(p), end=reinterpret_cast<std::uintptr_t>(m.BaseAddress)+m.RegionSize;
 return x<=end && n<=end-x;
}
bool executable(std::uintptr_t p) {
 MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION m{};
 if (!p || !VirtualQuery(reinterpret_cast<void*>(p),&m,sizeof(m)) || m.State!=MEM_COMMIT || (m.Protect&(PAGE_GUARD|PAGE_NOACCESS))) return false;
 DWORD prot=m.Protect&0xff;
 return prot==PAGE_EXECUTE || prot==PAGE_EXECUTE_READ || prot==PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE || prot==PAGE_EXECUTE_WRITECOPY;
}
void eventHook(void* queue,void** slot) {
 if (!ready.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) { realQueue(queue,slot); return; }
 void* event=nullptr; std::uintptr_t vt=0, destroy=0;
 unsigned char kind=255, action=0, pressed=0;
 // The vtable and tag must both match the mouse factory. Never suppress or
 // interpret any keyboard, touch, text, or unknown event as a mouse event.
 bool mouse=slot && read(slot,&event,sizeof(event)) && event && readAt(event,0,vt) && vt==image+mouseVtableRva &&
   readAt(event,8,kind) && kind==0 && readAt(event,0x18,action) && readAt(event,0x19,pressed);
 if (!mouse) { realQueue(queue,slot); return; }
 const bool menu=menuOpen.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
 unsigned bit=pressed<=1 ? menu_mouse::buttonBit(action) : 0, old=0;
 if (bit) old=pressed ? held.fetch_or(menu?0:bit,std::memory_order_acq_rel)
                      : held.fetch_and(~bit,std::memory_order_acq_rel);
 if (!menu || (pressed<=1 && menu_mouse::allowMouse(true,action,pressed!=0,old))) { realQueue(queue,slot); return; }
 // Queue takes a unique pointer and invokes the first virtual deleting
 // destructor if it still owns it. Do the same when discarding an event.
 if (!writable(slot,sizeof(*slot)) || !read(reinterpret_cast<void*>(vt),&destroy,sizeof(destroy)) ||
     destroy<image || destroy-image>=0x1a91000 || !executable(destroy)) {
  // Do not send an untrusted click into the world. In this abnormal case we
  // deliberately leak the event rather than execute an unverified destructor.
  return;
 }
 *slot=nullptr;
 reinterpret_cast<DeleteFn>(destroy)(event,1);
}
// If a button was already held when the menu opened, enqueue its UP edge so
// the world does not continue mining/attacking. The object and queue are taken
// from the live handler on its own tick; nothing is cached or fabricated as a
// press. Race-safe with a physical up edge reaching eventHook at the same time.
void releaseHeld(void* handler) {
 std::uintptr_t queue=0; std::int16_t x=0,y=0;
 if (!readAt(handler,0x20,queue) || !queue || !readAt(handler,0x12a,x) || !readAt(handler,0x12c,y)) return;
 unsigned bits=held.exchange(0,std::memory_order_acq_rel);
 for (unsigned action=1;action<=3;++action) if (bits&menu_mouse::buttonBit(action)) {
  unsigned char button=static_cast<unsigned char>(action), up=0;
  std::uint32_t relative=1; void* event=nullptr;
  factory(&event,&button,&up,&relative,&x,&y);
  if (event) realQueue(reinterpret_cast<void*>(queue),&event);
  else held.fetch_or(menu_mouse::buttonBit(action),std::memory_order_acq_rel);
 }
}
std::uintptr_t tickHook(void* handler) {
 if (!ready.load(std::memory_order_acquire) || !handler) return realTick(handler);
 unsigned char grabbed=0; std::uint32_t command=0;
 auto* commandPtr=static_cast<unsigned char*>(handler)+0x74;
 if (!readAt(handler,0x72,grabbed) || grabbed>1 || !readAt(handler,0x74,command) || command>2 || !writable(commandPtr,sizeof(command))) {
  return realTick(handler);
 }
 const bool menu=menuOpen.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
 auto d=cursor.step(menu,grabbed!=0,command,GetTickCount64());
 if (menu && held.load(std::memory_order_acquire)) releaseHeld(handler);
 if (d.command!=command) std::memcpy(commandPtr,&d.command,sizeof(d.command));
 return realTick(handler);
}
}
void SetMenuMouseOpen(bool value) { menuOpen.store(value,std::memory_order_release); }
int MenuMouseStatus() { return ready.load(std::memory_order_acquire)?1:0; }
bool InitializeMenuMouse(HatCreateHook create,HatToggleHook enable,HatToggleHook disable,HatToggleHook remove) {
 // ChinaHatAvailable means the shared verifier has checked the complete disk
 // SHA256, PE identity and its own loaded signatures. Verify our sites too.
 if (!ChinaHatAvailable() || !create || !enable || !disable || !remove) return false;
 image=reinterpret_cast<std::uintptr_t>(GetModuleHandleW(nullptr));
 if (!image) return false;
 for (const auto& sig:signatures) {
  unsigned char bytes[16]{};
  if (!read(reinterpret_cast<void*>(image+sig.rva),bytes,sizeof(bytes)) || std::memcmp(bytes,sig.bytes,sizeof(bytes))!=0) return false;
 }
 factory=reinterpret_cast<FactoryFn>(image+factoryRva);
 visual_hooks::Hook hooks[]={
  {reinterpret_cast<void*>(image+queueRva),reinterpret_cast<void*>(&eventHook),reinterpret_cast<void**>(&realQueue)},
  {reinterpret_cast<void*>(image+tickRva),reinterpret_cast<void*>(&tickHook),reinterpret_cast<void**>(&realTick)}
 };
 if (!visual_hooks::install(hooks,2,create,enable,disable,remove)) return false;
 ready.store(true,std::memory_order_release); return true;
}

// Full replacement of the adapter's game menu, built on RmlUi (HTML/CSS with

// Pure window-layout math for the windowed in-game menu. No engine includes:
// the adapter (menu_rml.cpp) and the Linux pixel harness both call this, so
// the tiling that ships is exactly the tiling that was verified.
//
// Contract: computeMenuWindows() packs the windows left-to-right into rows
// (a new row starts whenever the next window would not fit the viewport
// width), rebalances a lonely last row, centers every row and the block, and
// scales row heights down proportionally (window bodies scroll) when the
// natural heights do not fit. Windows in their default positions never
// overlap each other and never leave the viewport.
#pragma once

namespace menu_layout {

struct WindowRect {
    float x;
    float y;
    float w;
    float h;  // unfolded height actually shown (<= natural height)
};

constexpr float kMargin = 28.0f;
constexpr float kGap = 14.0f;
constexpr float kMinRowHeight = 200.0f;
constexpr int kMaxRows = 8;
constexpr int kMaxWindows = 16;

// row_of[i] receives the row index of window i; row_count receives the number
// of rows. Greedy first-fit in window order: a window only joins a row when
// the row's width with it still fits the viewport, so rows never overflow
// horizontally (except a single window wider than the viewport itself).
inline void packRows(const float* natural_w, int count, float avail_w,
                     int* row_of, int& row_count) {
    row_count = 1;
    float row_w = 0.0f;
    for (int i = 0; i < count; ++i) {
        if (row_w == 0.0f) {
            row_w = natural_w[i];
        } else if (row_w + kGap + natural_w[i] <= avail_w) {
            row_w += kGap + natural_w[i];
        } else {
            row_count++;
            row_w = natural_w[i];
        }
        row_of[i] = row_count - 1;
    }
}

// Move trailing windows down while the last row is much emptier than the one
// before it, so a 6+1 split becomes 5+2 and 4+3 instead of an orphan.
inline void rebalanceLastRow(const float* natural_w, int count, float avail_w,
                             int* row_of, int& row_count) {
    while (row_count >= 2) {
        int last = 0, prev = 0, last_start = -1, prev_last = -1;
        float last_w = 0.0f, prev_w = 0.0f;
        for (int i = 0; i < count; ++i) {
            if (row_of[i] == row_count - 1) {
                last++;
                if (last_start < 0) last_start = i;
                last_w = (last == 1) ? natural_w[i] : last_w + kGap + natural_w[i];
            } else if (row_of[i] == row_count - 2) {
                prev++;
                prev_last = i;
                prev_w = (prev == 1) ? natural_w[i] : prev_w + kGap + natural_w[i];
            }
        }
        if (last_start < 0 || prev_last < 0 || last >= prev - 1 || prev <= 1) break;
        if (last_w + kGap + natural_w[prev_last] > avail_w) break;
        row_of[prev_last] = row_count - 1;
    }
}

inline void computeMenuWindows(const float* natural_w, const float* natural_h, int count,
                               float view_w, float view_h, WindowRect* out,
                               float right_inset = 0.0f) {
    // right_inset reserves a strip along the right edge (the 3D preview
    // window lives there); the tiled block centers inside the remaining
    // width so it stays visually centered on the whole screen.
    const float avail_w = view_w - 2.0f * kMargin - (right_inset > 0.0f ? right_inset : 0.0f);
    const float avail_h = view_h - 2.0f * kMargin;

    int row_of[kMaxWindows] = {};
    int rows = 1;
    packRows(natural_w, count, avail_w, row_of, rows);
    if (rows > kMaxRows) rows = kMaxRows;
    rebalanceLastRow(natural_w, count, avail_w, row_of, rows);

    float row_natural[kMaxRows] = {};
    for (int i = 0; i < count; ++i) {
        const int row = row_of[i];
        if (row < kMaxRows && row_natural[row] < natural_h[i]) row_natural[row] = natural_h[i];
    }

    // Hand out the vertical space: every row keeps at least kMinRowHeight
    // while space lasts; above that, rows grow proportionally to their
    // natural height. If even the minimums do not fit (tiny viewport), the
    // rows scale purely proportionally so the block always fits exactly.
    const float room = avail_h - (rows - 1) * kGap;
    float row_height[kMaxRows] = {};
    const float min_total = rows * kMinRowHeight;
    if (room >= min_total) {
        float excess_total = 0.0f;
        float excess[kMaxRows] = {};
        for (int r = 0; r < rows; ++r) {
            excess[r] = (row_natural[r] > kMinRowHeight) ? row_natural[r] - kMinRowHeight : 0.0f;
            excess_total += excess[r];
        }
        const float room_excess = room - min_total;
        const float scale = (excess_total > 0.0f && room_excess < excess_total)
                                ? room_excess / excess_total
                                : 1.0f;
        for (int r = 0; r < rows; ++r) row_height[r] = kMinRowHeight + excess[r] * scale;
    } else if (room > 0.0f) {
        float natural_total = 0.0f;
        for (int r = 0; r < rows; ++r) natural_total += row_natural[r];
        const float scale = natural_total > 0.0f ? room / natural_total : 1.0f;
        for (int r = 0; r < rows; ++r) row_height[r] = row_natural[r] * scale;
    } else {
        for (int r = 0; r < rows; ++r) row_height[r] = kMinRowHeight;
    }

    float block_h = (rows - 1) * kGap;
    for (int r = 0; r < rows; ++r) block_h += row_height[r];
    float y = kMargin + (avail_h - block_h) * 0.5f;
    if (y < kMargin) y = kMargin;

    for (int r = 0; r < rows; ++r) {
        int in_row = 0;
        float row_w = 0.0f;
        for (int i = 0; i < count; ++i) {
            if (row_of[i] != r) continue;
            row_w = (in_row == 0) ? natural_w[i] : row_w + kGap + natural_w[i];
            in_row++;
        }
        // Center inside the strip-free area [0, view_w - right_inset] so no
        // row can ever reach into the reserved strip. With no inset this is
        // identical to the previous centering inside the margined viewport.
        float x = (view_w - right_inset - row_w) * 0.5f;
        if (x < kMargin) x = kMargin;
        for (int i = 0; i < count; ++i) {
            if (row_of[i] != r) continue;
            out[i].x = x;
            out[i].y = y;
            out[i].w = natural_w[i];
            out[i].h = (natural_h[i] < row_height[r]) ? natural_h[i] : row_height[r];
            x += natural_w[i] + kGap;
        }
        y += row_height[r] + kGap;
    }
}

// Clamp a dragged window so its title bar always stays reachable.
inline void clampDraggedWindow(WindowRect& rect, float view_w, float view_h) {
    const float keep_w = 90.0f;
    if (rect.x < keep_w - rect.w) rect.x = keep_w - rect.w;
    if (rect.x > view_w - keep_w) rect.x = view_w - keep_w;
    if (rect.y < 0.0f) rect.y = 0.0f;
    if (rect.y > view_h - 46.0f) rect.y = view_h - 46.0f;
}

// True when no pair of the first count rects overlaps. Windows are compared
// on their shown (unfolded) height; the caller passes folded windows with
// their title-bar-only height (46px).
inline bool rectsOverlap(const WindowRect* rects, int count) {
    for (int i = 0; i < count; ++i)
        for (int j = i + 1; j < count; ++j) {
            const bool apart_x = rects[i].x + rects[i].w <= rects[j].x + 0.01f ||
                                 rects[j].x + rects[j].w <= rects[i].x + 0.01f;
            const bool apart_y = rects[i].y + rects[i].h <= rects[j].y + 0.01f ||
                                 rects[j].y + rects[j].h <= rects[i].y + 0.01f;
            if (!apart_x && !apart_y) return true;
        }
    return false;
}

}  // namespace menu_layout

// RmlUi-based replacement of the adapter's game menu. The document markup and
// styling come from menu_rml_data.h; this translation unit:
//
//  - creates one RmlUi context with the vendored DX11 render interface on the
//    same device the legacy overlay already renders through (the back-buffer
//    render target view is passed in by the caller; RmlUi binds it during
//    EndFrame and restores the DirectX state afterwards);
//  - feeds input from the existing adapter hooks (patchedPointer, the UWP
//    wheel, the legacy key state export), never from new game hooks;
//  - maps switches and sliders one-to-one onto the adapter's existing,
//    verified setters (SetChinaHatEnabled, SetVisualParam, and
//    ag::Runtime::SetModule through the queued compat bridge);
//  - lays the menu out as independent windows: each window is dragged by its
//    title bar (RmlUi drag events), folds to its title bar, scrolls inside
//    when the viewport is small, and the default tiling (menu_layout.h)
//    never overlaps windows, whatever the number of functions.
//
// Failure of anything above only means the new menu stays hidden and the
// previous interface keeps working.
namespace menu_rml {
namespace {

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Cross-thread input and state plumbing (mirrors the previous menu embed).
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

std::atomic<bool> g_gameMenuOpen{false};
std::atomic<bool> g_hiddenByClose{false};
std::atomic<bool> g_hudEditorRequest{false};
std::atomic<bool> g_pointerValid{false};
std::atomic<float> g_pointerX{0.0f}, g_pointerY{0.0f};
std::atomic<float> g_pointerW{0.0f}, g_pointerH{0.0f};
std::atomic<float> g_wheelX{0.0f}, g_wheelY{0.0f};
bool (*g_keyDown)(int) = nullptr;
bool (*g_moduleStateReader)(int) = nullptr;

// Toggles for the game's own HUD modules must run on the legacy GUI thread
// (ag::Runtime::SetModule is not documented as thread-safe), so the menu only
// queues them; the compat layer drains the queue each frame.
std::mutex g_pendingMutex;
std::vector<std::pair<int, bool>> g_pendingToggles;

// The menu's own copy of the game's HUD module flags (indexed by
// ag::ModuleId): it initializes from the live state once and then follows the
// user's toggles, because re-reading the game state every frame raced the
// queued SetModule calls and the switch visibly jumped back.
bool g_moduleShadow[ag::kModuleCount] = {};
bool g_moduleShadowReady = false;

bool g_ready = false;
bool g_initFailed = false;
std::atomic<bool> g_renderOk{false};

bool g_mouseStates[2] = {};
bool g_escState = false;

RenderInterface_DX11* g_renderer = nullptr;
Rml::Context* g_rmlContext = nullptr;
Rml::ElementDocument* g_menuDoc = nullptr;
Rml::Element* g_ttStatus = nullptr;
Rml::Element* g_ttDiag = nullptr;
unsigned g_width = 0, g_height = 0;
bool g_menuShown = false;
// Document fade: frames left to keep rendering after the menu closed (the
// fade-out transition needs them).
constexpr unsigned kFadeOutFrames = 12;
unsigned g_fadeOutFrames = 0;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Window manager state: the two menu windows with their natural sizes and
// live geometry. Positions are owned here (never read back from the DOM), so
// dragging and re-tiling cannot desync from what is rendered.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

// UI zoom: the menu ships at a 1080p reference size; on small windows the
// fonts and shapes read as pixel mush. Every px in the RCSS and every layout
// constant below is multiplied by this factor at load time.
float g_uiScale = 1.0f;
// Screen-pixel strip reserved on the right for the compat layer's 3D preview
// window (drawn by the game's ImGui pass, so it is NOT multiplied by
// g_uiScale; it matches the ImGui window's pixel size).
constexpr float kPreviewInsetPx = 356.0f;

float computeUiScale(unsigned width, unsigned height) {
    const float ref = std::fmax(static_cast<float>(height) / 1080.0f,
                                 static_cast<float>(width) / 1920.0f);
    // v7: v6's compact zoom times 1.6 (1080p = 1.0, floor 0.92, 4K = 1.6).
    const float scale = ref * 1.25f * 0.5f * 1.6f;
    if (scale < 0.92f) return 0.92f;
    if (scale > 1.6f) return 1.6f;
    return scale;
}

// Multiply every `<number>px` in the RCSS by the UI scale. 0px stays 0px;
// deg/percent values have no px unit and are left alone.
std::string scaleRcssPx(const char* rcss, float scale) {
    if (scale == 1.0f) return std::string(rcss);
    std::string out;
    out.reserve(std::strlen(rcss) + 1024);
    const char* p = rcss;
    const char* end = p + std::strlen(rcss);
    while (p < end) {
        // Match -?digits(.digits)? followed by 'px'.
        const char* numberStart = p;
        if (*p == '-' && p + 1 < end && *(p + 1) >= '0' && *(p + 1) <= '9') ++p;
        while (p < end && *p >= '0' && *p <= '9') ++p;
        if (p < end && *p == '.' && p + 1 < end && *(p + 1) >= '0' && *(p + 1) <= '9') {
            ++p;
            while (p < end && *p >= '0' && *p <= '9') ++p;
        }
        if (p + 1 < end && p[0] == 'p' && p[1] == 'x' && p > numberStart) {
            const double value = std::atof(std::string(numberStart, p - numberStart).c_str());
            char scaled[48];
            std::snprintf(scaled, sizeof(scaled), "%.2fpx", value * static_cast<double>(scale));
            out += scaled;
            p += 2;
        } else {
            p = numberStart;
            out += *p;
            ++p;
        }
    }
    return out;
}

struct WinDef {
    const char* id;
    const char* headId;
    float w;
    float h;
};

// Natural (reference 1080p) sizes; multiplied by g_uiScale at init. v7: the
// Visuals window is the same height as Home; its body scrolls inside.
const WinDef kWindows[] = {
    {"win-home",    "head-home",    300.0f, 750.0f},
    {"win-visuals", "head-visuals", 460.0f, 750.0f},
};
constexpr int kWindowCount = static_cast<int>(sizeof(kWindows) / sizeof(kWindows[0]));
constexpr float kFoldedHeightRef = 46.0f;  // title bar + borders (reference)
float kFoldedHeight = kFoldedHeightRef;    // scaled at init
// Window fold/unfold runs as a short C++ height interpolation (RmlUi has no
// keyframes, and animating an explicit height property from CSS would fight
// the layout math that owns the same property).
constexpr unsigned kFoldAnimMs = 150;

struct WinState {
    Rml::Element* el = nullptr;
    Rml::Element* head = nullptr;
    float w = 0.0f, h = 0.0f;      // natural size
    float x = 0.0f, y = 0.0f;      // current position
    float shownH = 0.0f;           // unfolded height after tiling caps it
    bool dragged = false;          // user moved it: keep the position
    bool folded = false;
    float grabDx = 0.0f, grabDy = 0.0f;
    // Fold animation: animFrom -> animTo over kFoldAnimMs while animActive.
    bool animActive = false;
    DWORD animStart = 0;
    float animFrom = 0.0f, animTo = 0.0f, animH = 0.0f;
};
WinState g_win[kWindowCount];
int g_zTop = 20;
std::string g_ttStatusCache;
std::string g_ttDiagCache;

// 3D preview toggle (Visuals window).
std::atomic<bool> g_previewOn{true};
Rml::Element* g_previewSwitch = nullptr;

std::vector<char> g_fontNormal;
std::vector<char> g_fontBold;

float clamp01(float v) { return v < 0.0f ? 0.0f : (v > 1.0f ? 1.0f : v); }

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Diagnostic log: appended next to this DLL as gayclient-menu.log, so init
// failures and RmlUi parse errors are diagnosable on the user's machine
// without a debugger.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

std::mutex g_logMutex;

void menuLog(const char* format, ...) {
    char path[MAX_PATH] = {};
    HMODULE module = nullptr;
    if (!GetModuleHandleExA(GET_MODULE_HANDLE_EX_FLAG_FROM_ADDRESS |
                                GET_MODULE_HANDLE_EX_FLAG_UNCHANGED_REFCOUNT,
                            reinterpret_cast<LPCSTR>(&menuLog), &module) || !module)
        return;
    const DWORD length = GetModuleFileNameA(module, path, MAX_PATH);
    if (length == 0 || length >= MAX_PATH) return;
    char* slash = std::strrchr(path, '\\');
    if (!slash) return;
    std::snprintf(slash + 1, MAX_PATH - (slash + 1 - path), "gayclient-menu.log");
    char text[512];
    va_list args;
    va_start(args, format);
    const int written = std::vsnprintf(text, sizeof(text) - 1, format, args);
    va_end(args);
    if (written <= 0) return;
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(g_logMutex);
    if (std::FILE* file = std::fopen(path, "a")) {
        std::fprintf(file, "[%10u] %s\n", GetTickCount(), text);
        std::fclose(file);
    }
}

// Routes RmlUi's own log (font/document/RCSS/render errors) into the file.
class MenuSystemInterface : public Rml::SystemInterface {
public:
    bool LogMessage(Rml::Log::Type type, const Rml::String& message) override {
        menuLog("rmlui(%d): %s", static_cast<int>(type), message.c_str());
        return true;
    }
};
MenuSystemInterface g_systemInterface;

// Menu percentages (0..100) to the adapter parameter ranges.
float percentToRange(float percent, float low, float high) {
    return low + clamp01(percent / 100.0f) * (high - low);
}
float rangeToPercent(float value, float low, float high) {
    if (high <= low) return 0.0f;
    return clamp01((value - low) / (high - low)) * 100.0f;
}

bool keyIsDown(int vk) {
    if (g_keyDown && g_keyDown(vk)) return true;
    return (GetAsyncKeyState(vk) & 0x8000) != 0;
}

void queueAgModule(int moduleId, bool enable) {
    const int index = moduleId;
    if (index >= 0 && index < static_cast<int>(ag::kModuleCount))
        g_moduleShadow[index] = enable;
    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(g_pendingMutex);
    if (g_pendingToggles.size() < 32) g_pendingToggles.emplace_back(moduleId, enable);
}

void syncModuleShadow() {
    if (g_moduleShadowReady || !g_moduleStateReader) return;
    for (int i = 0; i < static_cast<int>(ag::kModuleCount); ++i)
        g_moduleShadow[i] = g_moduleStateReader(i);
    g_moduleShadowReady = true;
}

bool shadowModule(int moduleId) {
    if (moduleId < 0 || moduleId >= static_cast<int>(ag::kModuleCount)) return false;
    return g_moduleShadow[moduleId];
}

enum class SwKind {
    AgModule, ChinaHat, Trail, Jump, Katana,
    ChFill, ChRainbow, TrFill, TrRainbow, JrRainbow
};

struct SwitchDef {
    const char* id;
    SwKind kind;
    int ag;  // ag::ModuleId for SwKind::AgModule
};

const SwitchDef kSwitches[] = {

    {"sw-fps", SwKind::AgModule, static_cast<int>(ag::ModuleId::Fps)},
    {"sw-cps", SwKind::AgModule, static_cast<int>(ag::ModuleId::Cps)},
    {"sw-clock", SwKind::AgModule, static_cast<int>(ag::ModuleId::Clock)},
    {"sw-keys", SwKind::AgModule, static_cast<int>(ag::ModuleId::Keystrokes)},
    {"sw-watermark", SwKind::AgModule, static_cast<int>(ag::ModuleId::Watermark)},
    {"sw-coords", SwKind::AgModule, static_cast<int>(ag::ModuleId::Coordinates)},
    {"sw-res", SwKind::AgModule, static_cast<int>(ag::ModuleId::Resolution)},
    {"sw-perf", SwKind::AgModule, static_cast<int>(ag::ModuleId::Cpu)},
    {"sw-perf", SwKind::AgModule, static_cast<int>(ag::ModuleId::Ram)},
    {"sw-modlist", SwKind::AgModule, static_cast<int>(ag::ModuleId::ActiveModules)},
    // Visuals window: one master checkbox per effect, inside its section
    // (v6 removed the duplicate master rows at the top of the window).
    {"sw-gfx-chinahat", SwKind::ChinaHat, 0},
    {"sw-gfx-trail", SwKind::Trail, 0},
    {"sw-gfx-jump", SwKind::Jump, 0},
    {"sw-kt-master", SwKind::Katana, 0},
    {"sw-ch-fill", SwKind::ChFill, 0},
    {"sw-ch-rainbow", SwKind::ChRainbow, 0},
    {"sw-tr-fill", SwKind::TrFill, 0},
    {"sw-tr-rainbow", SwKind::TrRainbow, 0},
    {"sw-jr-rainbow", SwKind::JrRainbow, 0},
};

const SwitchDef* findSwitch(const Rml::String& id) {
    for (const SwitchDef& def : kSwitches)
        if (id == def.id) return &def;
    return nullptr;
}

bool readSwitch(const SwitchDef& def) {
    switch (def.kind) {
        case SwKind::AgModule: return shadowModule(def.ag);
        case SwKind::ChinaHat: return ChinaHatEnabled();
        case SwKind::Trail: return TrailEnabled();
        case SwKind::Jump: return JumpEnabled();
        case SwKind::Katana: return KatanaEnabled();
        case SwKind::ChFill: return HatFillEnabled();
        case SwKind::ChRainbow: return HatRainbowEnabled();
        case SwKind::TrFill: return TrailFillEnabled();
        case SwKind::TrRainbow: return TrailRainbowEnabled();
        case SwKind::JrRainbow: return JumpRainbowEnabled();
    }
    return false;
}

void applySwitch(const SwitchDef& def, bool on) {
    switch (def.kind) {
        case SwKind::AgModule: queueAgModule(def.ag, on); break;
        case SwKind::ChinaHat: SetChinaHatEnabled(on); break;
        case SwKind::Trail: SetTrailEnabled(on); break;
        case SwKind::Jump: SetJumpEnabled(on); break;
        case SwKind::Katana: SetKatanaEnabled(on); break;
        case SwKind::ChFill: SetHatFillEnabled(on); break;
        case SwKind::ChRainbow: SetHatRainbowEnabled(on); break;
        case SwKind::TrFill: SetTrailFillEnabled(on); break;
        case SwKind::TrRainbow: SetTrailRainbowEnabled(on); break;
        case SwKind::JrRainbow: SetJumpRainbowEnabled(on); break;
    }
}

// One uniform percent scale for every slider: the DOM value is 0..100 and
// maps linearly onto the parameter's spec range, so 0% is always the spec
// minimum and 100% always the spec maximum. The user sees percentages
// everywhere and both track ends are always reachable.
float domFromParam(const SliderDef& def, float param) {
    const auto& spec = visualParamSpecs[static_cast<std::size_t>(def.param)];
    return rangeToPercent(param, spec.low, spec.high);
}

float paramFromDom(const SliderDef& def, float dom) {
    const auto& spec = visualParamSpecs[static_cast<std::size_t>(def.param)];
    return percentToRange(dom, spec.low, spec.high);
}

const SliderDef* findSlider(const Rml::String& id) {
    for (const SliderDef& def : kSliders)
        if (id == def.id) return &def;
    return nullptr;
}

// Readout id: "sl-xxx" -> "ro-xxx".
Rml::String readoutIdFrom(const char* sliderId) {
    Rml::String out(sliderId);
    if (out.size() >= 2) out[1] = 'o';
    return out;
}
